messages:
lee: Quick heads-up — ran a small bring-up of a beam-hybrid speculative decode + early-abort on llama3-34b-q4_k_m. Putting raw notes here so we can triage before a larger holdout.
sam: nice. high level numbers?
lee: short summary: median token latency ~2.6x lower vs baseline greedy q4_k_m, p95 ~1.8x lower. Throughput improved ~2.3x for batch=8. Quality: small regressions on some factual QA slices (~0.8% EM drop) and a larger hit on arithmetic/chain-of-thought style prompts (~1.9% acc). Dialogue fluff and summarization unchanged.
marta: can you paste the decode config you used? especially early-abort rule.
lee: sure — config we A/B'd (copy):

```yaml
model: llama3-34b-q4_k_m
decode:
  mode: hybrid-beam-speculative
  beam_width: 3
  speculative: true
  speculative_ratio: 0.6    # prob mass threshold to trigger spec tokens
  early_abort:
    enabled: true
    min_confidence: 0.70    # abort speculative path when low conf
    patience: 2             # allow 2 tokens past low conf
kv_prefill: true
kv_warmup_frac: 0.8
batch_size: 8
``` 
lee: early-abort implements a running softmax-entropy check + max token prob. If max_prob < min_confidence for more than patience tokens, abort the speculative path and fallback to canonical beam decoding for the remaining tokens.
devon: how did you measure quality? standard eval sets? paired comparisons?
lee: used our internal eval harness: TruthfulQA (slice), MCQA math subset, and a 5k internal dialog holdout. For significance we ran paired bootstrap on per-example scores; the factual QA drop is not significant (p~0.12) but math drop is significant (p~0.03). Also saw cluster of failures when prompts had long numeric sequences — looks like speculative path beats itself into a bias.
sam: interesting. any telemetry on KV staleness / cache misses? I worry spec + prefill interacting weirdly with KVC.
lee: saw slightly higher KV invalidations on long context (>2048 tokens) — speculative path sometimes emits tokens that cause later attention patterns we didn't anticipate. Increased KV churn by ~6% on long sessions. Might be related to the speculative_ratio setting.
marta: let's plan holdouts: 1) early-abort-only (no hybrid beam), 2) beam-hybrid-only (no early-abort), 3) full spec (both), plus baseline. Run each for 100k queries across slices and compute paired bootstrap and ROC on confidence -> correctness.
sam: +1. Also add variant with lower speculative_ratio (0.4) and a stronger min_confidence (0.8). That might trade more latency for quality.
lee: noted. I can spin the A/B jobs. Quick numbers from the canary (2k queries each) attached here:

```text
baseline (greedy q4_k_m): median=42ms, p95=120ms, accuracy(math)=78.4
spec-beam+early: median=16ms, p95=67ms, accuracy(math)=76.5
spec-beam-only: median=18ms, p95=72ms, accuracy(math)=77.1
early-only: median=30ms, p95=95ms, accuracy(math)=77.8
``` 
devon: rollback/fallback plan for production?
lee: yes — rollout will be canary on 2% traffic with automatic rollback if math accuracy drop >1.0 absolute and p<0.05 in paired test, or if p95 latency regression > +10% on non-spec baseline. Also auto-fallback per-request: if model_confidence < 0.5 after speculative attempt, route to conservative decoder path.
marta: I'll run the ablations and push per-slice diffs. If math stays bad, maybe add special-case deterministic decoding for prompts matching numeric regex.
sam: good call. also add an eval that measures token-level hallucination spikes (we have heuristics) — speculative sometimes introduces short-width hallucination patterns.
deploy-bot: deploy.started for job spec-beam-holdout-1780012345 at 1780012405 by lee
lee: thanks — I'll post the full aggregated results when jobs finish (ETA ~3h). tagging @marta @sam @devon for visibility :eyes:
